newsitem.title: NORWAY: FOCUS - Norway's Aker books weaker profits.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Norway's Aker books weaker profits.

text.p: Norwegian industrial group Aker ASA on Thursday reported a 60 percent plunge in eight-months profit and blamed the earnings slump on its offshore construction subsidiary Norwegian Contractors.

Pre-tax profits for January to August plunged to 216 million crowns ($33.17 million) from 538 million in the same year-ago period -- prompting a 0.4 percent fall in Aker A shares to 128.50 crowns in morning trade.
Operating profit dropped to 28 million crowns from 234 million. Earnings per share fell to 3.48 crowns from 8.19, but sales rose to 5.55 billion crowns from 5.37 billion.
"The drop in profits is mainly due to a marked downturn in Norwegian Contractor's profits after a particularly good year in 1995," a company statement said.

Aker, which agreed this month to merge with fishing-based RGI to create one of Scandanavia's largest industrial groups, said its two main business areas, cement and buildings materials as well as oil and gas technology, had developed positively.

Aker said the period had been eventful. The company had decided on a merger between its subsidiary Aker Oil and Gas Technology and Maritime Group ASA, proposed a fusion between Aker and investment group RGI and settled the Sleipner claim.

Norwegian Contractors was building Sleipner's concrete gravity base for state oil company Statoil when the offshore platform sank in a fjord near Stavanger in 1991. Aker last month settled a dispute with the Insurance Group on the platform.

The eight-month group figures included a negative effect after financial items of just under 100 million crowns resultng from the Sleipner settlement but also gains in excess of 100 million crowns from the sale of fixed assets.
Aker said its board of directors had unanimously appointed Bjoern Rune Gjelsten as new president and chief executive of Aker ASA.
Gjelsten, 40, a co-founder of RGI and current chairman of Aker, will take up the position when current president and chief executive Tom Ruud steps down on November 1 as planned.
The boards of Aker and RGI on October 1 proposed to merge operations after RGI acquired more than 30 percent of Aker shares last spring.
Subject to approval by shareholders next month, the merger will create an industrial group with annual revenues of 19 billion crowns and a market capitalisation of nine billion.
The combined company, Aker RGI ASA, will focus on three core areas -- seafood, cement and oil and gas.

Aker said activity in the 33.3 percent Aker-owned Nordic cement and building materials company Scancem had increased after a slow start. Aker included 190 million crowns of Scancem profits in its accounts.

Aker Oil and Gas Technology's profit after financial items rose to 227 million crowns from 89 million. The division's order book totalled 7.3 billion crowns on August 31, up slightly from the start of the year.

Aker ASA and other activities, including Norwegian Contractors, made a loss after financial items of 201 million crowns versus profits of 294 million in the comparative 1995 period. ($1=6.512 Norwegian Crown)
